graft.title: rust profile's deny.yml: take the toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml
graft.need: The rust profile's deny.yml template installs its toolchain with `uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, which pins a second toolchain beside rust-toolchain.toml, against the profile's own rule rust.ci-reads-toolchain. Replace that step with `- run: rustup toolchain install` (comment: the toolchain, components and targets rust-toolchain.toml pins), as autodyne's deny.yml has done since 2fb442c. Every other line of the template stays as it is.
graft.use_case: `tend check` in autodyne warns baseline.rendered: .github/workflows/deny.yml edited by hand. The edit is this one step. Once the template has it, a plain render clears the warning, and every Rust project's deny job gets the toolchain its rust-toolchain.toml pins (sylva's rendered deny.yml still uses dtolnay@stable).

answer.text: Done (batch 01a19334-3d3d): the rust profile's deny.yml runs `rustup toolchain install` (commented as you asked) in place of dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable. One difference from autodyne's file: the step carries `working-directory: {{product.folder}}`, because the template checks the project out into that folder, and rustup reads rust-toolchain.toml from where it runs. It reaches you with the next release (after 2026.10.6). A plain render then gives the same step plus that working-directory line, which clears the baseline.rendered warning.
